behavior.text: The playback study tested whether male Diana monkeys distinguished familiar from unfamiliar male callers during responses to predator-specific alarm calls at Taï Forest and Tiwai Island. At both sites, acoustic features of responses varied with caller familiarity, but the direction of the familiar-versus-unfamiliar pattern differed between sites. The authors also report that familiarity affected leopard-induced alarms at Taï but not at Tiwai.

behavior.placeTimeScope: Wild Diana monkeys at Taï Forest, Côte d’Ivoire (N=20, August to December 2013), and Tiwai Island, Sierra Leone (N=23, January to March 2014); playback observations and conclusions are restricted to these two study populations.
behavior.lifeStatus: Wild adult male Diana monkeys and their alarm-call responses; no captive or domesticated animals are included. The study does not assess development, reproduction, or lifespan.

interactions.text: The study examined male-to-male responses to familiar and unfamiliar conspecific alarm callers that signal leopard or eagle stimuli. Its site-specific playback results support a bounded observation about social signaling and predator-associated alarm contexts, not a population-wide measure of predation risk or a complete interaction network.
